questions.q: What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of −5?
questions.why: 5 = 00000101; flip to 11111010; add 1 to get 11111011. (10000101 is −5 in sign and magnitude.)

questions.q: 01100100 is shifted left by 1 place in an 8-bit unsigned register. What happens?
questions.why: 01100100 is 100. A left shift doubles it to 200 = 11001000, which still fits in 8 bits (0 to 255), so no overflow.

questions.q: Explain why hexadecimal is often used instead of binary by programmers.
questions.model: Hexadecimal is much shorter than binary because one hex digit represents 4 bits, so it is easier for people to read and remember and there are fewer errors when copying it. It also converts easily to and from binary.
points: shorter / more compact than binary (one hex digit = 4 bits)
easier for humans to read, remember or copy, so fewer errors
easy to convert to and from binary
